title: Garden and Spire Again
premise: Ivo Eastwick flees her hedge-witch master into the one valley where magic cannot follow, only to have a dying stranger press a map into her hands and die at her feet. The map leads to the court beneath the mountain, where a usurper holds stolen souls as collateral for his armies — including the soul of the stranger's sister, sold years ago to buy the free cities a false peace. Hunted by the usurper's inquisitors and shadowed by Wren, a disgraced court knight who owes the stranger his life, Ivo must learn that the valley didn't strip her of magic but taught her to carry it silently. In the mountain's heart she discovers the usurper is himself soulless, a hollow man sustained by what he has taken, and that returning the souls will unmake him — and possibly her. Ivo trades her own name-soul to anchor the stolen ones home, defeats him, and walks out of the mountain unnamed but loved, choosing justice over the law that would have hanged them both.
about_author: Marguerite Kavanagh is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval land deeds before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about ordinary people caught between institutions and their consciences, and lives with an ill-tempered cat named after a disputed border town.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. She runs from her master's cottage into the magic-dead valley, tasting freedom for the first time — until a bloodied stranger stumbles from the pass, presses a folded map into her hands, and dies whispering a name: Sarelle. Ivo buries him and tells herself to walk away. Emotional beat: guilt curdling into reluctant obligation; the map won't leave her alone, literally warming against her skin.

chapters.title: What the Map Wants
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The map pulls her eastward through country she's never seen; when she tries to burn it, it reassembles in her pack. She's caught by Wren, a knight gone grey and drunk since his patron's death, who recognizes the stranger's seal and demands the map. She refuses; he follows instead. Emotional beat: two wary strangers bound by a dead man, neither trusting the other's reasons.

chapters.title: Inquisitors on the Road
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The usurper's inquisitors reach the border towns, burning records and questioning anyone who knew the dead courier. Wren recognizes their methods — he once served beside them — and realizes Ivo is already marked. He saves her from a checkpoint by lying badly and running well. Emotional beat: Wren's shame at his old obedience; Ivo's first taste of being hunted for something she never chose.

chapters.title: The Free Cities' Bargain
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They reach Merrowgate, where the free cities' council debates appeasing the usurper. Ivo learns the truth: twenty years ago the cities bought peace by selling souls to the mountain court, Sarelle among them. The council wants the map destroyed and the past buried. Emotional beat: Ivo's fury at respectable people choosing comfort over justice; Wren confronting the institution he still half-loves.

chapters.title: Sarelle's Room
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Following the map's second layer, they find Sarelle — alive, aged wrong, her eyes empty, kept as a trophy in a merchant's house under a binding contract. Ivo can't free her without the original deed held beneath the mountain. Sarelle briefly surfaces and begs her not to come. Emotional beat: love as evidence — the stranger died for this; Ivo stops asking whether she should go and starts planning how.

chapters.title: The Hollow Court
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. They infiltrate the mountain through the miners' stair Wren helped seal years ago. Inside, the court is beautiful and wrong: servants with borrowed faces, music with no players. Wren sees what the usurper's power costs and understands why he fled service. They're discovered by the chamberlain, who offers Wren his old rank to betray Ivo. Emotional beat: temptation of restoration versus integrity; Wren chooses Ivo and the run begins.

chapters.title: The Deed of Names
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. In the archive of contracts, Ivo finds every soul-deed — including a blank page bearing her own name, waiting. The valley didn't erase her magic; her master sold her potential here long ago, which is why the stranger sought her out. The usurper arrives, courteous and terrible, and offers her everything if she signs willingly. Emotional beat: betrayal by the person who raised her; the horror of discovering your escape was always someone else's design.

chapters.title: What the Usurper Lost
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Cornered, Ivo reads the deeds aloud and learns the usurper's secret: he signed away his own soul first, and everything since has been a hollow man's hunger to feel real again. Wren buys time with a duel he cannot win. Ivo realizes returning the souls will collapse the court — and that someone must stay behind to anchor them, a living name to hold the door. Emotional beat: pity for the monster; terror crystallizing into resolve.

chapters.title: The Mountain's Heart
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Climax. Ivo offers her own name-soul as the anchor, speaking the valley's silent magic — the discipline of holding power without letting it use you. The souls pour home; the usurper, offered his own deed back, chooses instead to shatter the court rather than face being small and mortal. The mountain groans; Wren drags a fading, nameless Ivo toward daylight as the contracts burn. Emotional beat: sacrifice answered by love; power refused at the moment it was finally offered.

chapters.title: A Name Worth Earning
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Weeks later, in the free cities, the soulless are waking and the council scrambles to claim credit. Sarelle, restored, tends Ivo's slow recovery — names return like scar tissue, piece by piece. Wren stands trial for desertion and is acquitted by the same crowd he once policed; justice outside the law, imperfectly done. Ivo takes a new name, hers by choice. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — duty transformed into chosen belonging, and a life begun again on honest terms.
